articles.title: PINTEREST RESTYLE REIMAGINES YOUR ROOM
articles.summary: Pinterest has unveiled Restyle, an AI-powered feature that lets users upload a photo of their room and explore how different design ideas would look in their own space. Users can test furniture, decor, paint colors, and lighting, remove or swap individual objects, or try a completely different style. Launching in beta in the US and Canada, Restyle brings Pinterest Intelligence directly into the consumer experience, helping people compare options and turn inspiration into more concrete plans for their homes.

articles.title: SAMSUNG STARTS ROLLING OUT ANDROID 17 WITH ONE UI 9, CONFIRMS INITIAL LIST OF GALAXY DEVICES
articles.summary: Samsung has officially begun rolling out One UI 9, based on Android 17, starting with the Galaxy S26 series after a four-month beta. The update introduces new Galaxy AI features, including My FanCam, Creative Studio, Now Brief enhancements, improved privacy and security tools, and easier access to warranty information. Samsung says the update will gradually expand to more Galaxy phones and tablets, including recent S-series, Fold, Flip, and Tab models.

articles.title: PUBLISH WEAVE TOOLS TO THE FIGMA COMMUNITY
articles.summary: Figma now lets users build custom Weave tools—generative AI workflows created in Figma Weave—and publish them to the Figma Community for others to use directly on the canvas in Figma Design. These tools support repeatable image and vector generation at scale, and people can browse the Community to see tools others have built. While any output type, including video and 3D renderings, can be published to the Community, only image and vector generation tools work within Figma Design itself.

articles.title: SEVEN LINES OF CLIENT FEEDBACK THAT KNOCK YOU SIDEWAYS, AND HOW TO STOP THEM LIVING RENT-FREE IN YOUR HEAD
articles.summary: Clients often give confusing or unhelpful feedback because of uncertainty, internal politics, or a lack of design knowledge rather than problems with the work itself. Common situations include vague requests like “make it look less designed,” Canva comparisons, hidden budgets, feedback by committee, and indecisive comments such as “I'll know it when I see it.” Responding with calm questions, clarifying underlying concerns, setting expectations early, and guiding clients through the design process can turn frustrating feedback into more productive conversations.

articles.title: FIVE ERAS OF UX DESIGN AND THE LESSONS TO KEEP IN THE AI ERA
articles.summary: User experience design has evolved through five major eras—from Human Factors and the Web to Mobile, Design Systems, and AI—each contributing a lasting lesson while leaving behind habits that later became limitations. Designers should focus less on producing interfaces and more on shaping systems, information architecture, constraints, and the rules that govern intelligent experiences, as these are becoming the most valuable skills in the AI era. Rather than replacing UX, AI continues the historical pattern of making creation cheaper while shifting designers' value toward higher-level thinking and decision-making.

articles.title: THE INVISIBLE SIDE OF DESIGN ENGINEERING
articles.summary: Design engineering has no fixed definition, and social media makes it look like little more than building animated eye-candy components. Day-to-day work leans heavily on invisible priorities like accessibility, responsiveness, performance, and the edge cases only real users surface. A great experience often comes down to unglamorous effort, like spending an afternoon on an accessibility fix or making a landing page load slightly faster.

articles.title: CURATED COLORS IN CONTEXT
articles.summary: Happy Hues is a color palette inspiration site that acts as a real-world example of how the colors could be used in your design projects.

articles.title: KNOW YOUR SHORTCUTS
articles.summary: An interactive 3D keyboard for learning the keyboard shortcuts of the apps you use every day. Pick a tool, hover a shortcut, and watch the keys light up.

articles.title: WHY CANVA HIT THE BRAKES ON ITS HUGE AI ROLLOUT (AND WHAT OTHER BRANDS CAN LEARN FROM IT)
articles.summary: Canva revealed that overwhelming demand for Canva AI 2.0 forced it to pause the rollout, leading the company to re-engineer the platform and reduce AI processing costs by nearly 90% while making it five times faster. Rather than relying on a single AI model, Canva is investing in a diverse AI strategy focused on delivering reliable, affordable, and user-friendly experiences that can adapt as AI technology evolves.

articles.title: FITTS'S LAW: WHY THE EASY BUTTON WINS
articles.summary: Fitts's Law, developed from 1954 cockpit-control research, holds that reaching a target gets faster as it grows larger and slower as it sits farther away. Screen edges and corners act as "magic pixels" that are effectively infinite in size on desktop, while touchscreens replace that trick with a thumb-reachable zone. The same principle for making desired actions easy to click can be inverted into dark patterns, like oversized subscribe buttons next to tiny cancel links.

articles.title: PLANNING WITH AGENTS: DIVIDED WORLDS, BOUNDARY OBJECTS, AND THICKER INTERFACES
articles.summary: Current agent-planning interfaces trap people in walls of Markdown text, even though humans read roughly 240 words a minute against an agent's 4,500. Chuukese wayfinding and Susan Leigh Star's boundary-object theory frame a case for thicker, visual, interactive, and social interfaces instead of thin text exchanges. A GitHub Next prototype called Chopin explores multiplayer, real-time planning where coworkers and agents share visual, editable plans rather than solitary text approvals.

articles.title: HOW ROB FARMER TURNS HALF-BAKED SKETCHES INTO NEW YORK TIMES COVERS
articles.summary: Australian motion designer Rob Farmer turns everyday observations into experimental design work, encouraging creatives to share imperfect ideas and embrace curiosity over perfectionism.

articles.title: ARTIST TURNS RENAISSANCE PAINTINGS, DIGITAL FRAGMENTS, AND DREAM LOGIC INTO SURREAL WORLDS THAT FEEL MORE LIKE MEMORIES THAN COLLAGES
articles.summary: Since 2009, self-taught Canary Islands artist Chema Mendez has fused Renaissance paintings, photography, and AI-generated details into surreal collages that feel like resolved dream paintings, not fragments.

articles.title: AI MIGHT KILL HUMANITY IN 10 YEARS, BUT AUTODESK'S CEO SEES A MORE IMMEDIATE THREAT TO ARTISTS
articles.summary: Autodesk CEO Andrew Anagnost calls the industry's AI-extinction talk partly "political theater" while still insisting the technology needs real guardrails.
